title: Salmon poke bowl
equipment: Medium saucepan with a tight lid (or a rice cooker)

items: 8–10 oz sushi-grade salmon, skin removed, kept cold

steps: Buy salmon sold as sushi-grade or for raw eating, from a fish counter you trust. Keep it in the fridge until the moment you cut it.

Rinse the rice in a strainer under cold water, swishing it with your hand, until the water runs mostly clear, about 1 min. Put it in a saucepan with 1¼ cups water and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook 15 min. Turn off the heat and rest 10 min, still covered.
Stir 1 Tbsp rice vinegar, the sugar and salt until dissolved. Gently fold it into the warm rice and let it cool to just warm, about 10 min.
While the rice rests, cut the salmon into ¾-inch cubes with a sharp knife. In a medium bowl, toss it with the soy sauce, sesame oil and 1 tsp rice vinegar. Cover and refrigerate 10–30 min.
Slice the cucumber, avocado and scallions.
Divide the rice between 2 bowls. Arrange the salmon, cucumber and avocado on top and sprinkle with scallions.
Spoon on the chili crisp and drizzle the Japanese mayo in lines. Eat right away.
tips: Put the salmon in the freezer for 15 min before cutting. It firms up and cubes cleanly.
Can't find sushi-grade fish? Use cooked salmon or cooked shrimp instead of raw.
Short on time? Use plain warm white rice with a splash of rice vinegar.
storage: Raw fish does not keep. Eat poke the day you make it, and keep the cut salmon cold until you serve it. Leftover plain rice keeps 4 days in the fridge if cooled within 2 hr.
